title.value: Poisson Midpoint Method for Log Concave Sampling: Beyond the Strong Error Lower Bounds

abstract.value: We study the problem of sampling from strongly log-concave distributions over $\mathbb{R}^d$ using the Poisson midpoint discretization (a variant of the randomized midpoint method) for overdamped/underdamped Langevin dynamics. We prove its convergence in the 2-Wasserstein distance ($\mathcal W_2$), achieving a cubic speedup in dependence on the target accuracy ($\epsilon$) over the Euler-Maruyama discretization, surpassing existing bounds for randomized midpoint methods. Notably, in the case of underdamped Langevin dynamics, we demonstrate the complexity of $\mathcal W_2$ convergence is much smaller than the complexity lower bounds for convergence in $L^2$ strong error established in the literature.

primary_area.value: probabilistic methods (Bayesian methods, variational inference, sampling, UQ, etc.)
